environmentNotes: Server and client are NOT kept running — start them yourself in the background when a check needs them (server: npm run start:dev from server/, client: bun run dev from client/, http://localhost:5173). This applies on the host; inside a Claude sandbox container (scripts/claude-docker, see docs/knowledgebase/docker-dev-container.md) they are already running — do not start them again. Temp files go in tmp/ (gitignored), never in the project root. The scenarios-* checks (npm run test:scenarios) build and start their own isolated stand (own port, own scn_* schema in DATABASE_URL, needs Postgres and — for mode b — Mailpit, e.g. docker compose -f tests/scenarios/docker-compose.yml up -d); they do not depend on the dev server and never touch it. Iterative runs (finalRun false) are the FAST SET: every `static` check plus `build` — no DB, no stand, no dev app. contract, scenarios-a/b/c, e2e-fast and e2e-full are finalOnly and run only in the final verification. While iterating on behaviour, run just the touched scenario: npm run test:scenarios -- --mode <a|b|c> --only scenarios --grep "<@S-TAG>". Work Hub (work-hub/, a separate Rust + bun product) has its own work-hub-* checks: they need Rust 1.92 (work-hub/rust-toolchain.toml), bun 1.4.4 and `npm ci` in work-hub/ plus `bun install` in work-hub/web/. work-hub-contract and work-hub-scenarios-a/b/c also need Docker running (they create containers, volumes and images labelled with their own instance and remove them afterwards), Postgres and — for mode b — Mailpit from the same tests/scenarios/docker-compose.yml; the first run builds the default container image artisyn-work-hub-default (npm run image in work-hub/, needs the network once) and the fake-agent test image, later runs reuse them.

checks.name: build
checks.instructions: Zero compilation errors allowed across all packages. Runs first in the `app` group because it rewrites server/src/public/static/*, which the watched dev backend reloads on — it must never overlap an e2e run.

checks.name: e2e-fast
checks.instructions: Fast @core loop (<3min). Drives the running dev app and the real DB — the `app` group keeps it serial with the build and the other suites.

checks.name: e2e-full
checks.instructions: Full suite — run once right before declaring a work cycle done, not every iteration. Drives the running dev app and the real DB — the `app` group keeps it serial with the build and the other suites.

checks.name: scenarios-a
checks.instructions: Isolated stand in auth mode none: run.mjs builds tmp/scenarios/stand/, starts its own server on a free port in a fresh scn_* schema and drops it afterwards — it does not use or touch the dev server, the dev DB's public schema or server/src/public/static (the run fails if either changed). Exit 2 = preflight (Postgres/Mailpit/Chromium/stray tmp/scenarios/.env.local) — fix the environment, not the tests. The stand build rewrites the installer in place like npm run build, hence the `app` group. Mode A is the big integrated run (~13 min in Oct 2026) and is kept as ONE check on purpose — raise the budget rather than splitting it by --grep, which could silently drop a scenario whose tag no split covers.

checks.name: contract
checks.instructions: Isolated: jest -c jest.contract.config.js boots its own app on a free port in a fresh contract_<uuid> schema (loaded with the world-v1 fixture, dropped afterwards) and never touches the dev server or the dev DB's public schema. Needs only Postgres. It shares Postgres with the server tests and e2e, hence the `app` group. A failing registry row prints its id, route, actor and every response-vs-SQL difference; the meta-test (routes.contract-spec.ts) lists every router route without a row — add the row to server/test/contract/registry/* (see server/test/contract/README.md), never loosen the meta-test. Jest's 'did not exit one second after the test run' warning alone is NOT a failure — judge by the exit code.

checks.name: client-typecheck

Note tsc reports only the first incompatible property of an object literal at a time: after fixing one, re-run, as more may surface behind it.

The first run compiles the Cargo workspace into work-hub/target, hence the long budget; later runs are incremental.
